title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو  يستنكر المذابح في ليبيا ويناشد الجميع حقن الدماء
title_en: His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew Condemns the Massacres in Libya and Appeals to All to Spare Blood
body_ar: في اتصال مع قناة الجزيرة زوال اليوم الموافق ل 20 فبراير 2011، استنكر الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء المجازر التي تحدث هذه الأيام في ليبيا، وناشد كل أحرار العالم أن يقفوا مع الشعب الليبي الأعزل، ويستنكروا ما يحدث له من قتل ومصادرة للحريات، وأكد على أنه من حق الشعب الليبي أن يعبر عن رأيه بطرق آمنة وسلمية، مضيفا "لو كان الشعب بالفعل هو من يحكم ليبيا كما يتغني بذلك النظام لوقف مع المواطنين ولما ترك المجازر ترتكب بحقهم". وناشد الشيخ -حفظه الله- السلطات الليبية بإيقاف المجازر ضد شعبها فقد كفى قتلا لو كان يجدي، محذرا من مخاطر إشاعة الفتنة والاستعانة بمن أسماهم "حثالة ممن جاؤوا يطلبون الدريهمات" بدل إتاحة حرية التعبير التي تكفلها القوانين للجميع. كما استنكر فضيلته التعتيم الإعلامي وسياسة تكميم الأفواه، وأكد أن ما يحدث الآن جريمة ومنكر وسيحاسب عليه التاريخ، ولن يجدي نفعا، مطالبا الجزيرة بأن توصل للرأي العام كلما توصلت به من أنباء، وأن تكثف اتصالاتها حتى تُجلي الحقيقية للناس.
body_en:
In a call with Al Jazeera at midday today, 20 February 2011, Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, condemned the massacres taking place in these days in Libya, and appealed to all the free people of the world to stand with the unarmed Libyan people and to condemn the killing and the seizure of liberties being visited upon them. He affirmed that it is the right of the Libyan people to express their opinion by safe and peaceful means, adding: "If the people were in fact the ones governing Libya, as the regime sings, it would have stood with the citizens and would not have left massacres to be committed against them."

The Sheikh — may God preserve him — appealed to the Libyan authorities to halt the massacres against their own people, for there has been killing enough, were killing of any avail; and he warned of the dangers of spreading strife and of calling in those whom he termed "dregs who have come seeking a few dirhams", instead of allowing the freedom of expression that the laws guarantee to everyone. His eminence also condemned the media blackout and the policy of muzzling mouths, and affirmed that what is happening now is a crime and a wrong for which history will call to account, and that it will avail nothing. He called upon Al Jazeera to convey to public opinion every piece of news that reaches it, and to intensify its contacts so as to make the truth plain to people.

flags.note: Editorially sensitive under style guide section 12, and the sensitivity is specific rather than general: this is a named, dated condemnation of a particular government's conduct, made on air on 20 February 2011, in the opening days of the Libyan uprising. Its meaning depends entirely on that date and that moment, and in English, undated, it reads as a standing political position. Nothing has been softened, sharpened or omitted, including the quoted phrase about 'dregs who have come seeking a few dirhams'. The date must be displayed with it. This is also the one record in this slice whose CMS timestamp is corroborated by its own text, which says 'today, 20 February 2011'.

flags.context: the Sheikh's own quoted phrase, as the site reports it
options: dregs who have come seeking a few dirhams
riff-raff who came for a handful of money
flags.note: 'الدريهمات' is the diminutive of dirhams and carries contempt for the smallness of the sum; 'a few dirhams' keeps that. 'Mercenaries' would be the natural English word for what is being described in the events of February 2011, but the Sheikh does not use it, and the summary explicitly marks the phrase as his own wording ('those whom he termed'). The literal rendering is used so that his words are not replaced by a term of art he did not choose.

flags.context: the closing call to Al Jazeera
options: read as 'الحقيقة' (the truth) and translate accordingly
flags.note: 'الحقيقية' is written with an extra yāʾ where 'الحقيقة' is intended. Left as served in body_ar; recorded rather than silently corrected.

translator_notes: A site news summary of a live broadcast intervention, not a text by the Sheikh. Everything attributed to him is the site editor's report of what he said by telephone, except the two passages the report puts in quotation marks; the English keeps that distinction visible.
